title: Une chance pour Samy  (A Chance for Samy)

segments.t: At a Parisian cafe, agent Mathias Barneville meets his star client Gerard Lanvin to discuss shooting dates. Noticing that their ambitious young waiter Samy dreams of acting, Gerard suggests giving him a screen test for a bodyguard role. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Samy, viens voir une minute.
Oui, monsieur Barneville, j'arrive.
Tu veux toujours faire du cinéma?
Oui, c'est mon grand rêve!
Tu veux passer un casting?
Un casting? Vous êtes sérieux?
C'est pour mon film À cran.
As-tu un CV et des photos?
J'ai tout dans mon sac.
Apporte-les tout de suite.
Vous réalisez mon rêve aujourd'hui!
Attention, ce sont juste des essais.
Si tu réussis, le rôle est à toi.
Merci, je vais donner le meilleur!
Let's observe as Gerard and Mathias offer Samy a screen test for the movie.
Samy, viens voir une minute.
'Samy, come see for a minute.' Notice how 'come' leads directly into the noun meaning 'minute'. Notice how 'come' leads directly into the noun meaning 'minute'.

'Yes, Mr. Barneville, I am coming.' The verb meaning 'arrive' pairs naturally with the noun for 'Mr.' in everyday conversation.

'Do you still want to do cinema?' In everyday spoken French, rising intonation on 'want' at the end is enough to turn the sentence into a question. In everyday spoken French, rising intonation on 'want' at the end is enough to turn the sentence into a question.

'If you succeed, the role is yours.' A conditional encouragement motivating the young actor. The informal 'you' form around 'succeed' marks a direct, personal relationship.
